## feature

### five error-stats summary tables reshaped to one-row-per-reference

```
level: high
```

#### reason

A value-level test pins every schema and hand-computed expectations for all
five tables, and a CLI smoke run reproduced the same numbers on a real BAM.

#### description

```
type: [table, text]
```

1. `deletion`/`insertion`: `seq_name, total, {del,ins}_a.._t` plus one rate
   per base, normalized inside the sequence.
2. `per_base`/`per_read`: `seq_name, total, insertion, deletion, mismatch`
   plus one rate per count (the old `substitution` label became `mismatch`).
3. `mismatch`: 16-row substitution/accuracy matrix (below).
4. `error`, `single_deletion`, `ref_summary` outputs are unchanged.

| Table | Rows per ref | Rate denominator |
|---|---|---|
| deletion | 1 | per-seq event total |
| insertion | 1 | per-seq event total |
| per_base | 1 | aligned bases |
| per_read | 1 | tallied reads |
| mismatch | 16 | row total (see item) |

#### before

All five tables were long-format `(seq_name, type, count)` or a 4-column
matrix; consumers re-aggregated them downstream to compare references.

#### after

One row per reference answers each QC question directly; rates use the
existing 0.0-on-zero-denominator convention.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_stats.py::test_error_stats_summary_table_schemas` asserts all
  five column sets and values from the hand-computed read
  `:4*ac+gt-cg:2` over `ACGTACGTAC`.
- 160 tests, ruff, and pyright green this session.

:::

### mismatch table carries adf/adr, match diagonal, and norm_rate

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The strand test pins the split with balanced and asymmetric substitutions;
the no-accessor test pins the null behavior; the smoke run showed adf/adr
values matching hand computation on a real forward+reverse pair.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `adf`/`adr` split each cell's count by FLAG 0x10 — the same vocabulary
   as `pileup`, so a strand-balanced substitution keeps `adf ≈ adr` while
   an artifact does not.
2. The `ref == alt` diagonal carries strand-split inner-region match
   observations (per-reference prefix counts: O(1) per `:` op, not a
   per-base loop).
3. `rate = (adf+adr) / seq mismatch total` (null on the diagonal);
   `norm_rate = (adf+adr) / row total` — the conditional
   P(read base | ref base) with the reference-composition exposure divided
   out (the `AAACGT` motivation).
4. N read-base mismatches count in the row total without a row.

#### before

The table was a 4x4 matrix of event counts; composition bias favored
abundant reference bases, and no strand or match information existed.

#### after

The table is a complete per-amplicon substitution/accuracy matrix; each
row's `norm_rate` values sum to at most 1, and the diagonal reads as
per-base accuracy.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_stats.py::test_error_stats_mismatch_strand_split`: A->T
  `(adf 1, adr 1)`, A->G `(1, 0)`, diagonal A->A `(4, 2)` with
  `norm_rate 2/3`.
- Smoke run this session: forward `:4*ac+gt-cg:2` + reverse `:4*ac:5` →
  A->C `(1, 1)`, A->A diagonal `(2, 2)`, rate null on the diagonal.

:::

### error-stats requires --fasta

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The CLI help shows FASTA as required (verified in the fresh-env install),
all fixture-updated tests pass, and the release notes state the migration.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `ErrorStatsArgs.fasta` is non-optional; `run_error_stats` opens the
   FastaFile unconditionally.
2. `smoothed_deletion` is always populated via the CLI; the null branch
   remains only for library users constructing the collector without a
   reference accessor.
3. qc-summary and pileup fasta options are unchanged.

#### before

A fasta-less run produced three nullable behaviors (smoothed_deletion, and
would have produced null diagonals and norm_rates); consumers had to know
which mode produced a file.

#### after

Every CLI-produced file is fully populated; the reference is a required
input, matching the fail-fast default.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Fresh-env `sam-tagger error-stats --help` (deployed package) shows
  `INPUT-BAM CONFIG FASTA` in the usage line.
- `tests/test_validation.py` error-config tests now pass fasta fixtures.

:::

## limitation

### norm_rate corrects composition bias, not position-level hotspots

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The row-total conditioning is exact for the abundance question by
construction; the hotspot caveat follows from the tally design (per-position
error clustering is visible only in error.parquet), not from a measurement.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `norm_rate` removes the first-order reference-composition bias.
2. Clustered errors (homopolymers, strand gradients) still skew per-base
   comparisons; per-position evidence lives in `error.parquet` and
   `pileup`.
3. The adf/adr aggregate cannot locate a strand bias to a position —
   `pileup`'s per-position adf/adr covers that.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/usage.qmd` error-stats section documents the row-total semantics
  and the N-in-denominator convention.

:::

### requiring fasta does not verify it is the right fasta

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The warn-once disagreement path predates this change and remains the only
cross-check between the fasta and the cs-deleted bases.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. A mismatched reference silently shifts match counts and norm_rate.
2. The existing warning (fasta base vs cs-deleted base) fires once per run;
  it does not validate matched positions at all.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py` `_smooth_deletion` warning branch.

:::

## assumption

### strand balance indicates true substitutions

```
level: low
```

#### reason

The adf/adr interpretation rests on PCR mixing strands; this is standard
variant-calling practice, but this repo's own data has not been used to
validate the expected balance distribution.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Reading `adf ≈ adr` as "true substitution" assumes strand-balanced
   amplification.
2. The test to confirm or refute: compare adf/adr splits against known
   synthetic variants in an ecsngsqc run.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

None

:::

## process

### halted the release mid-flight and re-cut the tag after the design dialogue

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The user stopped the v0.7.0 release after the tag push; four design
   turns followed (norm_rate, diagonal matches, required fasta, adf/adr).
2. The stale tag and its auto-created release were deleted, the work
   landed as two commits, and the tag was re-cut at the final commit.
3. This kept the released 0.7.0 artifact identical to the final spec —
   no version was shipped twice with different content.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `gh release delete v0.7.0` + tag delete/re-create in this session's
  history; final tag at `cecfb73`.

:::

### bulk text substitution broke test files twice

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. A scripted insertion of `assert setup.fasta_path is not None` after
   every config assert landed at wrong indentation inside a nested block
   and hit tests that pass no fasta.
2. The suite caught both (IndentationError, then a None assert), but each
   cost a repair round.
3. The better action: per-site Edit calls with the surrounding context,
   or a scoped script keyed on the exact call sites — not a file-wide
   pattern replace.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `IndentationError` at `tests/test_integration.py` and the
  `test_qc_summary_cli` None failure, both this session.

:::
